description: Wiring |W|² in place of s² into the beta-decay rate multiplies every rate by |W(q0)|²/s²(q0) = 129.405107404 (half-lives by 0.00773): the prescribed substitution is a scope-(a) negative, not the 10–17 % heavy-nucleus correction attributed to it — the substituted half-lives land at 0.8–0.9 % of observed, ~110x too short. THE POWER WAS s⁴ AND THE FACTOR 1.19e4 UNTIL 2026-09-05: S_SQ is already s², so squaring it double-counted the amplitude; the rate carries s² once (prf:trace-ratio-observable). The verdict is unchanged, the magnitude is 92x smaller (bean qou-xql6). Also fixes the provenance of the two stale W values: both are hecke_division's former z^{len} trace rule, at z_C (0.7036, the published figure) and z_D (0.9684, the 2026-08-29 witness). Table 4 of ex:hadron-half-life-verification has no producer.

provenance.note: correction to docs/audits/2026-09-04-weak-vertex-t35-trace-closed-form.md, which attributed 0.7036 to the deprecated t35-full-calculation.py

assertions.name: factor_is_one_hundred_twenty_nine_at_proton_pin
assertions.note: |W|²/s² = 129.405107404; the Lean bound is substitutionRateFactor_near_one_hundred_thirty. This read 'between 1e4 and 2e4' until 2026-09-05 because FACTOR squared S_SQ, which is already s² (bean qou-xql6)

assertions.name: substitution_is_not_a_10_to_17_percent_correction
assertions.note: SCOPE-(a) NEGATIVE: every substituted half-life lands at 0.8-0.9 % of observed, i.e. ~110x too SHORT, where a 10-17 % shortening was wanted. Two-sided on the measured band so the gate fails if the numbers MOVE. (Read '< 0.1 %' until 2026-09-05, on the s^4 factor.)

assertions.name: published_0_7036_is_buggy_rule_at_zC
assertions.note: Σ c_w z_C^{|w|} over the reduced (σ₀σ₁)^5 — provenance of the published value

assertions.name: witness_0_9684_is_buggy_rule_at_zD
assertions.note: Σ c_w z_D^{|w|} — provenance of t35-weak-vertex.witness.json (2026-08-29)

assertions.name: patched_engine_matches_closed_form
assertions.note: hecke_division.markov_trace now delegates to the canonical recursion (float64 engine, 1e-12 tolerance)
